input: # divergence.tsv - inputs where the TypeScript and Go runtimes CLASSIFY OR
# VALUE THE SAME SOURCE DIFFERENTLY. Found by a differential probe over 1686
# distinct generated CSS-ish inputs (51 diverged); these are the minimal
# reproducers for the two classes found.
# AGENTS.md rule 1: "TypeScript is canonical. When TS and Go disagree, TS
# wins; change Go." The `expected` column below is therefore the OBSERVED TS
# behaviour, and every row is expected to FAIL in go/parity_test.go until Go
# is brought into line. That red is the point: these fixtures exist to make an
# invisible divergence visible, not to bless either answer.
# NOTE FOR THE FIX PHASE: pinning TS here follows the repo's authority rule,
# it is NOT an endorsement. For class B in particular there is a live
# question whether TS should strip comments from at-rule preludes the way it
# already strips them from selectors and declaration values (AGENTS.md
# "Declaration values and selectors are raw strings (trimmed, comments
# stripped)"), in which case the correct fix is to change TS and re-pin these
# rows -- not to change Go. Decide it deliberately; do not delete the rows.
# CLASS A - an UNTERMINATED /* inside an at-rule prelude.
#   TS accepts it as part of the raw prelude text; Go raises an unexpected-
#   character error. 27 of the 51 divergences were of this shape.
@import/*red
@import x/*y
@media screen/*y
@font-face~/*
# CLASS B - a TERMINATED comment inside an at-rule prelude / params.
#   TS keeps the comment text in the prelude string; Go strips it. Affects
#   every at-rule flavour: statement, rules-body, declarations-body and
#   keyframes. 24 of the 51 divergences were of this shape.
@import /*c*/x;
@media /*c*/screen{a{b:d}}
@page/*c*/x{a:b}
@keyframes /*c*/n{from{a:b}}
@supports /*c*/(a:b){c{d:e}}
@unknown /*c*/p;
